dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I humbly offer this prayer to our god: May the winds of the wild bring blessings upon you, washing away all your weariness and fatigue...

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: ...Eh, that'll probably do. I think I'll just skip the second half. This is supposed to be a break, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Hey, don't look so shocked. Since we're on a break, we might as well give the Archon a break too. He can't be listening to our prayers all the time!

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: You seem worried. Care to share what's on your mind? As a deacon, I'm quite good at helping people work through their troubles.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Mmm... Ahh... You're talking about how the deeper we go, the stronger the enemies we encounter? Yeah, I've noticed that, too.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: It definitely keeps things interesting and fun. But seriously, now that we've broken the ice — what is it that's troubling you?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Do you know what the best part of any story is? It's when the protagonist gets into big trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I love those moments when they're desperately trying to run away, and have to use every ounce of their wit to escape. Once the story goes in that direction, I'm hooked. Can't put the book down.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Still, most stories end the exact same way — with the protagonist finding their way out of the mess and living boringly ever after. I usually return the book before I get to that part.
